```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has sourced proof that money changes hands in its category. Acquire.com publishes $25-100/mo listing fees plus 6-8% closing fees, Flippa charges $29+ plus 5-10%, MicroExits takes 5% on close, and BuyMicroStartups charges a flat listing fee. Idea B's brief states outright that every competitor found is free and that there is 'zero price validation in the category.'",
    "The goal is one paying customer in 90 days. A seller-paid listing fee is a small, documented purchase that a single seller can make without the marketplace reaching full liquidity, and several comparables already collect such fees. Idea B must convert individual developers away from at least seven free tools, including nektos/act with 72k stars and GitLab's built-in debugging. The brief itself calls this audience 'one of the hardest' to convert.",
    "Idea A's brief names a concrete wedge: AI agents replacing the human 'acquisition expert' services that Acquire.com uses to justify its fees, aimed at sub-$10k deals. That is a paid service layer with a sourced price anchor. Idea B's differentiation (UX, multi-provider support, team features) has no evidence of willingness to pay. The competitor list shows the core feature has been cloned by hobbyists within months.",
    "Idea A's risks are serious but come with sourced numbers: buyer-side liquidity is weak, the $750 newsletter test produced zero sales, and 0%-commission rivals exist. Idea B's main risk, that no one pays, is the risk most directly fatal to a 90-day revenue goal, and nothing in its brief offsets it."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's price hypothesis of $15-20/month is anchored to Depot's $20/month single-developer plan. Depot is a different product category: hosted CI compute, not a local step-through debugger. The brief admits 'no exact paid comparable exists.' Willingness to pay therefore rests on one HN comment ('Solve this and I would pay for it'), against seven free alternatives.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs show crowded markets and weak conversion signals. Idea A faces a real two-sided cold-start problem, a failed $750 paid test, longer deal cycles before any closing fee arrives, and escrow and licensing setup. The deciding factor is that A has sourced evidence of paying users in its category while B has none. If one seller paying a listing fee is not reachable in 90 days, A's advantage shrinks considerably."
}
```
